Hey guys, wanting to start a garden in my backyard and wanted some ideas on where to start. Its coming into winter where i live (southern hemisphere) and its a pretty wet area, not swampy though.

What should i be starting at this time? any tips on vege arrangements or what plants to plant together or what fertilizers to use?

I tend to want to over-prepare for things before starting

If you are wet then build raised beds. Plant garlic and potatoes in them and cover them up with something (but leave holes for the garlic). The garlic and potatoes will grow over winter. building roots and making small tops. When the weather warms up and all the seeds sprout up under the covering and die then you can pull it off and plant other stuff in the same beds. I put lettuce and radishes and spinach and such in the spring. Then the garlic comes out mid-summer just when the potatoes are really getting going. I pick the spinach and kale and stuff like that and freeze it/eat it.

In another set of beds I also do garlic over winter but no potatoes. INstead I build a-frame trellises over the beds and plant tomatoe seeds under them, right between the garlic plants. The tomatoes get going about the same time the garlic finishes. So water it up and pull them.

Now the garlic needs to be put on a rack to dry for like 2-3 months in the shade. Leave the tops on it and rotate it a bit. If you get a lot of summer rains then you need it in a covered area or it will rot. I like to grow squash and pumpkins and all sorts of other shit as well but I always interplant it amongst garlic. If you can get horse poo, or rabbit poo or chicken or whatever mix it in to your soil in the FALL right before planting your garlic. Always rotate your crops. Dont leave the same thing in there for year after year or you may get disease problems. I like to leave beds fallow and just cover them with Buckwheat and red clover to recover for a season then till that in right before it goes to seed and then that bed is good to go. for next year. It takes time to get the bugs worked out... You will have weeds, other pests. I have gophers and mice. They are tricky. I have to put poision out for the mice and plant in raised beds with wire bottoms to beat the gophers. You may have caterpilliars or afids or some other god forsaken thing eating your shit. Good luck, its awesome. Get some Chickens as well.
